name: Self-Refine (iterative refinement with self-feedback)
exact_model: arXiv:2303.17651 (method record, not a servable model)
access: public preprint (arXiv); no weights, method only
license: Paper text CC BY 4.0; describes a prompting method with no released model weights.
context_tokens: not applicable (method record; depends on the host model)
serving_path: Not servable; a test-time generate-feedback-refine loop implemented over any host LLM (GPT-3.5/ChatGPT/GPT-4 in the paper).
game_research_use: Repair-precedent anchor for TRACE-RPG's counterexample-guided repair operator: Self-Refine is the canonical LLM self-repair loop, but its feedback is model-generated natural language and its evidence is live-model task-preference gains across 7 tasks (~20% absolute avg). TRACE-RPG's guided_repair arm differs on both axes: feedback is the validator's structured error set E, and evidence is deterministic fixture-level exact counts against blind-retry and state-reading-oracle arms.
key_risk: Reported gains are live-model, task-level, and preference/accuracy based; they do not transfer to claims about deterministic operator-level repair sufficiency, and Huang et al. (arXiv:2310.01798) report that intrinsic self-correction without external feedback can degrade reasoning performance.
evidence_status: verified-primary from the arXiv abstract page as of 2026-08-21.
uncertain: NeurIPS 2023 acceptance is widely indexed but was not re-verified against the NeurIPS proceedings for this record; cite as arXiv preprint unless proceedings are checked.
